input.public_request: Add an optional emoji marker before greeting output.

open_material_decisions: Exact output formatting when enabled, including spacing and whether the marker appears before all greeting variants.
How the optional emoji marker is controlled/enabled by the caller or configuration.
What emoji should be shown when the marker is enabled, if it is not caller-specified.

question.prompt: The way the emoji marker is enabled changes the API/CLI surface and default behavior. How should callers turn it on?

options.label: Explicit flag/param
options.description: Add a dedicated optional argument or setting to enable the emoji marker per greeting call; recommended because it keeps the feature reversible and clear.

options.label: Always on when configured
options.description: Use a global configuration setting so greetings include the emoji marker whenever that config is enabled.

options.label: Caller supplies prefix
options.description: Treat the emoji marker as a caller-provided prefix string rather than a built-in toggle, which is more flexible but broader in scope.

transcript.answer: {"selected_option":"Explicit flag/param","answer":"Callers should enable it per greeting call with a single optional boolean flag/parameter. When true, prepend exactly \"👋 \" to the existing greeting string; when false or omitted, leave the output unchanged."}

question.prompt: The specific emoji changes the visible output and acceptance criteria. Which built-in emoji should the optional marker use when enabled?

options.label: Wave hand
options.description: Use exactly `👋` as the built-in marker; recommended because it matches greeting semantics and the prior example.

options.label: Sparkles
options.description: Use exactly `✨` as the built-in marker; this is more decorative but changes the tone of the feature.

options.label: Custom per caller
options.description: Let the caller choose the emoji value each time; this is more flexible but expands scope beyond a simple optional marker.

transcript.answer: {"selected_option":"Wave hand","answer":"Use exactly \"👋\" as the built-in optional marker when enabled."}

interviewer.reason: No open material decision remains. The caller control, built-in emoji, and enabled-output formatting are all established by the transcript, and the request is implementation-ready without widening scope.

contract.summary:
Outcome: add an optional emoji marker before greeting output. Success means a caller can enable the marker per greeting call with a single optional boolean flag/parameter; when enabled, the greeting output is prefixed with exactly `👋 `, and when false or omitted, output remains unchanged.

In scope: one optional built-in emoji marker for greeting output, enabled explicitly per call. Out of scope: global config-driven behavior, caller-supplied arbitrary prefixes or emojis, and any other output changes.

Confirmed decisions: callers enable the feature with a dedicated optional flag/parameter per greeting call; the built-in marker is exactly `👋`; enabled formatting is exactly the existing greeting string prefixed with `👋 `.

Failure, edge, and misuse behavior: if the flag/parameter is false or omitted, behavior must match current output exactly; no alternative emoji or formatting should be inferred.

Constraints: preserve existing greeting behavior unless explicitly enabled; do not widen the API beyond a single optional boolean control.

Implementation authorization: not authorized by this interview alone.
confirmed_decisions: Use a dedicated optional boolean flag/parameter to enable the emoji marker per greeting call.
When enabled, use exactly `👋` as the built-in marker.
When enabled, prepend exactly `👋 ` to the existing greeting string.
When the flag/parameter is false or omitted, leave the greeting output unchanged.
acceptance_checks: A greeting call with the emoji flag/parameter omitted produces exactly the same output as before.
A greeting call with the emoji flag/parameter set to false produces exactly the same output as before.
A greeting call with the emoji flag/parameter set to true produces the prior greeting output prefixed with exactly `👋 `.
No global configuration or caller-provided prefix/emojis are required or introduced.

frozen_failure_lenses.failure_description: The request leaves "optional" undefined, so different readers cannot tell whether the marker is controlled per call, per user setting, or by a static default.
frozen_failure_lenses.observable_signal: Two reasonable implementers describe different activation conditions for when the marker appears, while both claim to satisfy the request.
frozen_failure_lenses.why_material: The handoff is not implementable if the trigger for the optional behavior is unclear.
frozen_failure_lenses.minimal_test_shape: Ask for the greeting output in two cases: with the option enabled and with the option not enabled; if the expected control point cannot be stated unambiguously, discovery failed.

findings.description: The transcript explicitly identified the affected greeting surface as still undecided, but the final contract closes all decisions and marks the handoff implementation-ready without resolving that boundary. The unresolved point was whether the marker appears "before all greeting variants," while the contract still speaks only in terms of generic "greeting output" / "greeting call."
